sections.title: The letter O
paragraphs: The letter (O) /oː/ is a vowel. A vowel is a sound made with open air. Its main sound appears in (Obst) /oːpst/, which means fruit. This letter has two sounds in German.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, pull your tongue back. Round your lips into a tight, small circle. Keep your lips steady and let your vocal cords vibrate. For the second sound, open your jaw slightly wider. Make a wider circle with your lips. Feel your throat shake for both sounds.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: You use the long sound in long or stressed open syllables. You hear it in (Sohn) /zoːn/. You use the short sound in short closed syllables. You hear it in (offen) /ˈɔfn̩/. Double consonants often follow this short sound, as in (Sonne) /ˈzɔnə/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not turn the long vowel into a diphthong. A diphthong is two vowel sounds that glide together. In English words like boat, your lips move. Keep your lips perfectly still until the sound ends. Do not say the short vowel like the vowel in hot. Keep your lips round and firm.
